title: Xreal Aura akıllı gözlük için ön siparişler açıldı
summary: Google ortaklığıyla geliştirilen şeffaf tasarımlı Xreal Aura akıllı gözlükler 1.279 dolardan başlayan fiyatlarla ön siparişe açıldı.
body:
Xreal, Google iş birliğiyle geliştirilen ve Android XR işletim sistemini kullanan ilk akıllı gözlük modeli **Xreal Aura** için fiyat ve çıkış detaylarını duyurdu. Ön sipariş süreci başlarken, cihazın sevkiyatlarının kasım ortasında ABD, Kanada, Japonya ve Güney Kore'de başlaması planlanıyor. Diğer pazarlara ise 2027 yılında açılması bekleniyor.

## Xreal Aura teknik özellikleri ve kullanım deneyimi

95 gramdan daha hafif olan Xreal Aura, şeffaf lensleri sayesinde kullanıcıların çevrelerini görmesine imkan tanırken sanal pencereler ve uygulamalar yansıtıyor. Gücünü Qualcomm tarafından geliştirilen Snapdragon Reality Elite çipten alan gözlük, işlemleri ve pil yönetimini ayrı bir kablolu kumanda kutusu (puck) üzerinden gerçekleştiriyor. Bu kutu üzerinde yerleşik bir izleme dörtgeni, parmak izi sensörü ve Android XR deneyimi yer alıyor.

Cihazda ayrıca Bose tarafından geliştirilen ses teknolojisi ve hassas el takibi bulunuyor. Xreal Aura iki farklı depolama ve bellek seçeneğiyle satışa sunuluyor: 12GB RAM ve 256GB depolama alanına sahip temel model ABD'de 1.279 dolardan başlarken, 16GB RAM ve 512GB depolama sunan üst versiyon ise 1.499 dolardan alıcı bekliyor.

**Neden önemli?** Xreal Aura, Android XR ekosistemini şeffaf lensli hafif bir tasarımla buluşturarak, kullanıcıların gerçek dünya üzerine sanal ekranlar ve uygulamalar yerleştirmesini sağlıyor.

source_texts.text:
XREAL's first Android XR glasses are almost as expensive as a Galaxy S26 Ultra
Oct 7, 2026 — 8:00 AM ET
- XREAL has announced pricing and availability details for its Aura Android XR glasses.
- These XR glasses start at $1,279 for a 12GB/256GB variant and start shipping in mid-November.
- The puck-powered glasses are equipped with built-in displays and an integrated trackpad.
XREAL is a leader in the XR glasses space, but it’s also been readying its first pair of Android XR glasses, dubbed the XREAL Aura. We already had a chance to go hands-on with these specs, but pricing and availability were a mystery. Until now, that is.
XREAL has announced that the Aura Android XR glasses will start at $1,279. This gets you the 12GB/256GB variant, while the 16GB/512GB model costs $1,499. The device is available in medium (60 to 66mm) and large (66 to 72mm) options. Either way, these glasses are slightly cheaper than the $1,400 Galaxy S26 Ultra was at launch, while being a scant $20 cheaper than Meta’s VR glasses.
Pre-orders are currently restricted to people who placed a reservation deposit, with XREAL adding that orders for the general public will open in the “coming weeks.” Can’t wait to get your glasses, but haven’t paid the deposit? The company says you can still pay the reservation deposit today for priority delivery.
The XREAL Aura glasses run Android XR and have a pair of built-in displays with a 70-degree field-of-view. This means you can do everything from watching YouTube to seeing Google Maps directions. The glasses also have a built-in trackpad for navigation, along with hand-tracking technology.
It’s worth noting that these glasses are powered by a Snapdragon Reality Elite chip in a bundled puck. So the tethered setup means it isn’t quite on par with something like Meta’s display-free Ray-Ban glasses when it comes to a lightweight experience.
In any event, the XREAL Aura glasses will start shipping in mid-November to customers in the US, Canada, Japan, and South Korea. Expect availability in more markets from 2027.

source_texts.text:
Two weeks ago, journalists in the San Francisco Bay Area got to try two hot new wearables that weigh only around 100 grams: the just-revealed Meta VR Glasses, and the long-awaited transparent Google XR glasses built in partnership with Xreal. It turns out they’re going head-to-head. Xreal has just opened Aura pre-orders starting at $1,279, $20 less than the Meta VR Glasses.
At $1,279, Google’s Xreal Aura will go head-to-head with Meta’s VR Glasses
The first transparent Android XR glasses are “weeks” away — if you made a reservation.
That’s for the Xreal Aura with 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage; there’ll also be a 16GB / 512GB config for $1,499. (Xreal couldn’t tell us whether the 16GB of RAM would be important for some apps by publish time.)
Both the Google / Xreal Aura and Meta’s VR Glasses let you overlay virtual objects and desktops on the real world. Both are relatively lightweight because they’ve got a cord — their Qualcomm Snapdragon Reality Elite chips and batteries both live in a compute puck, which runs either Meta’s Horizon OS or Android XR. Both greet you with a grid of floating app icons to choose from.
But they’re very different experiences in practice, primarily because the Google / Xreal Aura has transparent lenses, while the Meta VR Glasses use passthrough vision to let you see the real world and offers more immersion. While the Xreal Aura has one of the largest transparent fields of view yet at 70 degrees diagonal, it’s still smaller than Meta’s passthrough glasses. I wrote all about it in this story, and it’s just one of many differences.
The Meta VR Glasses also have eye tracking, like the Apple Vision Pro, so you can select things just by looking at them and pinching fingers resting on your lap; the Google / Xreal Aura has a touchpad built into the compute puck and hand-tracking to give you virtual laser pointers. (Both let you connect to other peripherals and display other devices too — and you can plug devices with USB-C DisplayPort video right in.)
And, of course, you’ve got your Android apps inside the Xreal Aura, or your Quest games inside the VR Glasses.
I don’t think any journalist can tell you which is better yet; you may want to wait for reviews. We also have yet to test Android XR extensively: while Samsung and Google did technically ship the $1,799 Galaxy XR with Android XR last year, they didn’t send one to The Verge for review.
The Meta VR Glasses aren’t due until spring 2027, but Xreal isn’t necessarily shipping lots of pairs before then. Today, the only people who can preorder the Xreal glasses are those who already put in a reservation, and only the first 2,000 “Founder’s Edition” pairs are necessarily coming at “launch.” Those will ship this year, Xreal CEO and co-founder Chi Xu tells The Verge.
It might not take till the end of the year. Xreal’s press release does say they “will begin shipping soon” and that the “launch” is “now just weeks away,” but those are wiggly, and again, those timeframes are just for early adopters. If you don’t have a preorder, “Orders will open to the general public in the coming weeks.” The glasses will also only ship in the US, Canada, Japan, and South Korea to start, before expanding to other regions in 2027.
I’m already a fan of Xreal’s glasses and how they let me watch my 3D movies with a 57-degree field of view, and I’m intrigued by the puck. I’d love to see how much more useful these glasses are with a 70-degree view.

source_texts.text:
Xreal's Aura Android XR smartglasses will cost you at least $1,279
The glasses are now available for pre-order.
Xreal has officially launched its Android XR-powered Aura smartglasses, which it introduced earlier this year at Google I/O. The device is now available for pre-order for those who've already paid a reservation deposit, with prices starting at $1,279. Aura weighs less than 95 grams, but it's a tethered model that attaches to a separate puck, which runs Android XR and comes with Google Play for apps, plus Gemini for AI capabilities.
The system uses the Snapdragon Reality Elite chip that Qualcomm designed to enable augmented and mixed reality capabilities in smaller and lighter headsets. Aura features precise hand tracking, thanks to its cameras, and has a 70-degree field of view. Its lenses are see-through, giving users a view of their surroundings outside what's projected on the virtual screen. We found its visuals extremely sharp and bright, even in sunny outdoor conditions, when we tested it at Google's developer conference. For audio, it uses Bose-engineered technologies.
In addition to providing compute power and Android XR experiences, the puck also has a built-in trackpad and fingerprint sensor, so you can use it for navigation. Xreal suggests carrying it on a lanyard or clipping it to the user's clothes or belongings. The glasses can also be plugged into a computer, however, if people want to use them as an external monitor.
Xreal's Aura will be available in two sizes: medium (60-66mm) and large (66-72mm). It ships with the compute puck and will come in two configurations, one with 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage and another with 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage. The bigger configuration costs $1,499. It will start shipping soon in the US, Canada, Japan and South Korea after orders open to the general public in the coming weeks. Xreal plans to release the model to more markets in 2027.
